prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1172; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recording is for our claim file. Can you state your full name for the record?

A: I'd rather just go by the claim number, if that's okay.

Q: That works for our purposes. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was stopped at a light on a main road in Sugar Land, near a shopping center. Traffic was moving slowly that afternoon.

Q: And what happened next?

A: I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest. The car behind me didn't stop in time.

Q: Did you get out of your vehicle right away?

A: I tried to, but I was dizzy and my neck was really stiff. A bystander helped me sit down on the curb until the paramedics arrived.

Q: Did you go to a hospital?

A: Yes, they took me by ambulance. They said I had a concussion. I've had headaches ever since, and bright lights bother my eyes.

Q: Are you still experiencing those symptoms?

A: Some days are better than others. I get tired by mid-afternoon and I've had trouble concentrating at work.

Q: Have you seen a doctor since then?

A: I've had two follow-up appointments and I'm scheduled for another next week. My doctor has me resting from screen time for now.

Q: Did you have any problems with your neck or back before this collision?

A: No, not that I can recall. I was driving to work normally and feeling fine.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add about the accident?

A: Just that I'm trying to get back to normal, and I appreciate you checking in on me.

Q: Thank you for your time today. We'll follow up with you soon.
